text_blocks.snippet: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) often presents with lower abdominal pain and abnormal vaginal discharge. Other symptoms include pain during sex, fever, chills, and pain or burning during urination. Some women may experience nausea, vomiting, or irregular bleeding. Many women with PID have no noticeable symptoms or mistake them for other illnesses.
snippet_highlighted_words: lower abdominal pain and abnormal vaginal discharge

list.snippet: Lower abdominal pain: This is the most frequent symptom, and it can range from mild to severe, and may worsen during sex or physical activity.
Abnormal vaginal discharge: The discharge may be yellow or green, and have an unusual odor.
Pain during sex: Painful intercourse, also known as dyspareunia, can be a sign of PID.
Fever and chills: These are signs of infection and can indicate a more serious case of PID.
